cards.claim: The next web wave would center on in-browser applications that feel like desktop software, powered by JavaScript techniques such as Ajax rather than static pages.
cards.outcome: Single-page and rich web apps became mainstream in email, docs, maps, and SaaS; XMLHttpRequest and later APIs underpin most interactive sites people use daily.

sources.label: WIRED (2011): Gmail popularized Ajax at mass scale
CNET (2005): Gmail and Google Maps as desktop-like Ajax apps
Wikipedia: Google Maps launched 2005 with JavaScript and Ajax

cards.claim: Startup funding would shift toward many smaller seed checks and angel-style rounds instead of relying on a few large VC gatekeepers.
cards.outcome: Seed and pre-seed activity expanded for years, with accelerators, angels, and micro-funds common—though late-stage capital also concentrated in mega-funds and growth rounds.

sources.label: PitchBook–NVCA Venture Monitor Q4 2023: U.S. pre-seed and seed deal counts and value
PitchBook–NVCA Venture Monitor Q4 2024: pre-seed/seed activity at 2024 highs

cards.claim: Even where the dot-com bubble burst, it would leave durable infrastructure—especially bandwidth and habits—that later startups could build on cheaply.
cards.outcome: Falling connectivity costs and global internet adoption supported mobile, cloud, and SaaS booms; many bubble-era fiber and hosting investments were later utilized at lower prices.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Dot-com bubble (aftermath and overcapacity)
OECD (2003): After the telecommunications bubble—fiber overbuild and price collapse
ITU Facts and Figures 2024: 5.5 billion people online (68% of world population)

cards.claim: The Segway would not replace cars or normal walking for most people because it looked awkward, needed special contexts, and did not fit everyday errands.
cards.outcome: Consumer Segway PT production ended; personal two-wheel devices stayed niche (tourism, security, warehouses) while cars and scooters dominated urban mobility.

sources.label: BBC News (June 2020): Segway PT production ends 15 July
CNN (June 2020): Segway stops manufacturing the Personal Transporter
Wikipedia: Segway PT (commercial history)

cards.claim: Microsoft would cease to be the dominant platform threat for startups because the action moved to the open web and Google-era services instead of the Windows API.
cards.outcome: Startups scaled on web, mobile, and cloud stacks with less Windows lock-in; Microsoft rebounded as a cloud and enterprise powerhouse rather than the default consumer platform gatekeeper.

sources.label: Microsoft FY2024 10-K (SEC): Intelligent Cloud segment revenue $87.5B
StatCounter: Mobile web usage exceeds desktop globally
Microsoft FY2024 10-K (SEC): Intelligent Cloud and Azure segment description

cards.claim: Apple's tight, centralized control of native iPhone apps through its store and approval process would become a strategic weakness versus more open platforms.
cards.outcome: Regulators and developers challenged App Store rules worldwide, yet Apple's ecosystem kept enormous revenue and user loyalty; openness moved partly to the web and sideloading debates, not a collapse of the model.

sources.label: U.S. Supreme Court docket: Apple v. Epic certiorari denied (Jan. 16, 2024)
CNBC (March 2024): EU DMA prompts Apple to approve Epic Games Store in Europe
European Commission DMA annual report 2024: App Store compliance investigations

cards.claim: Small, technology-driven companies could create large wealth quickly because software and automation let tiny teams serve huge markets—unlike many traditional small businesses.
cards.outcome: High-growth tech startups produced some of the largest market-cap gains of the 2000s–2020s, while most small firms remain local and modest in scale.

sources.label: First Trust (2025): Magnificent Seven drove most of S&P 500 2024 return
Mellon: Magnificent Seven combined market cap vs. Russell 2000 small caps

cards.claim: Returns in many competitive fields would keep skewing superlinear—small edges compounding so a few winners capture most of the upside in technology markets.
cards.outcome: Market concentration and winner-take-most dynamics strengthened in several digital sectors, though antitrust scrutiny and new platforms periodically disrupt incumbents.
